plan.title: 8-Week Intermediate Fat Loss Full Gym Plan

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.notes: As an intermediate with good muscle mass, focus on deep, controlled movements. Aim for a weight challenging enough by the last 2-3 reps. Start with 115-165 lb, adjusting as needed based on your current strength and form.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
exercises.notes: Emphasize hamstring stretch and glute contraction. Keep a slight bend in the knees and a flat back. Try starting with 95-135 lb.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.notes: Control the negative phase and avoid locking out your knees at the top. Use a weight where you feel a strong quad and glute engagement. Begin with 180-270 lb.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.notes: Focus on the quad squeeze at the top. Higher reps here promote metabolic stress for fat loss. Start with 70-100 lb.

exercises.name: Hamstring Curl (Lying or Seated)
exercises.notes: Isolate the hamstrings. Squeeze hard at the peak contraction. Begin with 60-90 lb.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.notes: Maintain a straight line from head to heels. Engage your core, avoid sagging hips. Hold for the recommended time.

exercises.name: Russian Twists
exercises.notes: Perform with or without a medicine ball. Focus on controlled rotation, not just arm movement. Try with a 10-20 lb medicine ball or bodyweight.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.notes: Focus on upper chest activation. Lower dumbbells with control, press powerfully. Start with 25-40 lb per hand.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.notes: Ensure proper arch and shoulder retraction for stability. Focus on a controlled descent. Start with 95-135 lb, adjusting for your strength level.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.notes: Press vertically, avoiding excessive back arch. Control the weight throughout the movement. Start with 20-30 lb per hand.

exercises.name: Lateral Raises (Dumbbell)
exercises.notes: Lead with elbows, maintain a slight bend in the arm, feel it in the side deltoids. Avoid shrugging. Begin with 10-15 lb per hand.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown (Rope or Bar)
exercises.notes: Fully extend the triceps, squeeze at the bottom. Keep elbows tucked close to your body. Start with 40-70 lb.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Flyes
exercises.notes: Focus on a deep stretch in the chest, with a slight bend in the elbows. Controlled movement is key. Try 20-30 lb per hand.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.notes: Focus on pulling with your back muscles, not just your arms. Squeeze shoulder blades at the bottom. Start with 80-120 lb.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.notes: Maintain an upright posture, pull to the lower abdomen. Feel the squeeze in your mid-back. Start with 80-120 lb.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-ups or Machine Pulldown (Close Grip)
exercises.notes: If performing assisted pull-ups, use assistance that allows for controlled reps. If using a machine, focus on back contraction. For assisted pull-ups, aim for 30-60 lb assist. For machine, use 70-110 lb.

exercises.name: Face Pulls
exercises.notes: Important for shoulder health and posture. Pull towards your face, externally rotating at the top. Start with 30-50 lb.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Rows
exercises.notes: Support yourself with one hand on a bench, keep your back flat and core engaged. Pull with the lats. Start with 30-45 lb per hand.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curls
exercises.notes: Control the eccentric (lowering) phase. Avoid swinging and maintain good form. Alternate arms or curl simultaneously. Start with 15-25 lb per hand.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell against your chest. Focus on depth and keeping your chest up. Use a 30-50 lb dumbbell or kettlebell.

exercises.name: Push-ups
exercises.notes: Perform on knees if needed, or elevate your hands to a bench for easier variation. Maximize reps with good form. This is a bodyweight exercise.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Rows (Alternating)
exercises.notes: Maintain a bent-over position with a flat back, engage your core. Pull one arm at a time. Start with 30-45 lb per hand.

exercises.name: Walking Lunges (Dumbbell)
exercises.notes: Take long strides, lower until your back knee almost touches the floor. Keep your torso upright. Hold 15-25 lb dumbbells per hand.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swings (American or Russian)
exercises.notes: Focus on powerful hip drive, not arm lifting. Hinge at the hips, explode forward. Start with a 25-45 lb kettlebell.

exercises.name: Mountain Climbers
exercises.notes: Maintain a strong plank position, drive knees to chest rhythmically. Keep core tight. Perform for the recommended time.
